names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 16 iulie, «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Atinoghen cu cei 10 ucenici ai săi», with the rank words left off.

Read out of saint.gr's line for 16 Ιουλίου, «Άγιος Αθηνογένης επίσκοπος Πηδαχθόης και οι Δέκα Μαθητές του», with the rank word, the see and the company left off. One of his ten disciples bears the same name on the same page, and the two are headed separately there.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 16. јул ст. ст., „Свешт. муч. Атиноген еп. Севастијски, у Јерменији.“ — „Свешт. муч.“ is one rank and „еп.“ the other, both of which `types` already carries, and „Севастијски, у Јерменији“ is the see that second rank governs and comes off with it, as „Тавроменијски“, „Гортински на Криту“ and „Едески“ did on 9 July. The bare forename is what is left. `foldchk.py` returns **no holder** and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts a new key with no other holder — which is worth recording, because `athenogenes-disciple-of-athenogenes` carries the identical English name and would have folded with this form the moment anybody gave him a Serbian one.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 16 iulie — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Atinoghen cu cei 10 ucenici ai săi»

attestations.note: The ten disciples are commemorated with him in the day's line and in the troparion, but neither the line nor the life names any of them, so they are kept here within his entry and not enumerated.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 16ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιος Αθηνογένης επίσκοπος Πηδαχθόης και οι Δέκα Μαθητές του»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 16 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own — bishop of Pedachthoe, taken with ten disciples in the persecution under Diocletian, beheaded. The Greek page adds three things. It gives his homeland as Sebastia in Cappadocia, where doxologia's life had the governor come to Sebaste without saying the bishop was from there. It gives the governor's name as Φηλίμαρχος, which doxologia's Romanian life writes Filomarh. And it names the ten disciples, whom doxologia's life leaves unnamed throughout — Ριγίνος, Μαξιμίνος, Πατρόφιλος, Αθηνογένης, Αντίοχος, Άμμων, Θεόφραστος, Κλεόνικος, Πέτρος, Ησύχιος — so the synaxis enumerates its members and the ten are drafted as ten folders in batch el-07-16-1. The page also heads him and each of the ten «(; - 311)», a year doxologia gave nowhere, and a `dates` object is proposed from it. It credits Athenogenes with the vesper hymn «Φῶς ἱλαρόν» and prints its text. There is a separate 16 Ιουλίου entry, «Άγιος Αθηνογένης *» at /2103/, which carries the asterisk and the «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence and says of itself «Μάλλον συγχέεται με τον Άγιο Αθηνογένη επίσκοπο Πηδαχθόης»: it is refused, and nothing from it is on this folder. This page itself carries no asterisk and no such sentence. It prints two apolytikia, both of which name him, and both are taken; the second is the common of a hierarch, «Κανόνα πίστεως, καὶ εἰκόνα πραότητος», printed under his name with his name sung into it, and is taken as a common and said here to be one.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 29.07.2026 (16. јул ст. ст.) — „Свешт. муч. Атиноген еп. Севастијски, у Јерменији.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. **THE IDENTIFICATION IS THE YEAR AND THE TEN DISCIPLES TOGETHER, NOT THE NAME.** The folder holds `death` 311, `attested`, and this book ends „и преселише се у небесну домовину, 311. год.“; the folder relates ten disciples and this body gives him ten; the Romanian and Greek rows stand on this very 16 July; and the heading ranks him „Свешт. муч.“ and „еп.“ where the folder holds `hieromartyr` and `bishop`. Four coincidences, of which **the ten and the 311 are the two that could not happen twice**. **AND THE TWO BOOKS GIVE HIM TWO DIFFERENT SEES.** This heading says „еп. Севастијски, у Јерменији“ — bishop of **Sebaste, in Armenia** — and the body has the persecutor Philomarchus coming **to Sebaste** and the monastery standing near that city. The folder’s display name is «Athenogenes of Pedachthoe» and its `office` is the bare «Bishop». **Nothing is changed.** §10 reserves a display name to the author; and the `office` is **not** improved to «Bishop of Sebaste», because that would quietly decide between two books in a field, which is exactly what a reader may not do — the folder’s own display name says Pedachthoe. Both readings go into the life and the difference is stated as a difference. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, THE YEAR CONFIRMED TO THE YEAR.** 311 against 311, and this book offers no age, no duration and no reign to refuse, Diocletian being named only as the time the persecutor came. `types` UNTOUCHED at `hieromartyr` and `bishop`, both earned by the heading. **`wonderworker` is not on offer**; **`abbot` is refused**, „Живљаше у једном манастиру“ putting him in a monastery and not over one. No `locations`: Sebaste, Armenia and Pedachthoe are a narrative, and the folder already carries a flat year. **TEN DISCIPLES, TEN FOLDERS, TEN FOLDERS STANDING ON THIS VERY NUMBER, AND NOT ONE ROW.** The body opens „Живљаше у једном манастиру близу града са 10 својих ученика“, he lived in a monastery near the city with ten of his own disciples, and **names none of them**. The corpus holds exactly ten: `ammon-disciple-of-athenogenes`, `antiochus-disciple-of-athenogenes`, `athenogenes-disciple-of-athenogenes`, `cleonicus-disciple-of-athenogenes`, `hesychius-disciple-of-athenogenes`, `maximinus-disciple-of-athenogenes`, `patrophilus-disciple-of-athenogenes`, `peter-disciple-of-athenogenes`, `reginus-disciple-of-athenogenes` and `theophrastus-disciple-of-athenogenes` — every one a `martyr`, every one with `death` 311, every one kept venerated by the Greek calendar on the **16 July**, every one relating this folder, and every one with an `undocumented` `serbian` row standing empty. **§4 and §5 decide it and the heading enumerates one person.** A row quotes the heading whole, the count is what the heading enumerates, and a heading that names nobody beyond its own subject gives one row. This is the largest such refusal of the whole range — ten folders in one day against the six monks of 5 July, the two of 6 July, the one of 7 July, the thirteen women of 8 July and the one soldier of 9 July — and it is the same refusal. **NO NEW `related` ROWS**, the ten being two-way already and Philomarchus a persecutor. **WHAT IS NEW IS A HIND AND A SENTENCE ABOUT BEASTS.** The persecutor told the old man to sacrifice to the idols so as not to perish as the other Christians had perished, and Athenogenes answered „о мучитељу, они које ти именујеш погинулим нису погинули него су на небесима и ликују с ангелима“ — O torturer, those you name as perished have not perished but are in the heavens and rejoice with the angels. **And then the hind.** A doe which the merciful Athenogenes had fed with his own hand ran to him and, seeing him in his distress, shed tears; „И зверови су горски имали више сажаљења према мученицима Христовим него незнабошци!“ — and the beasts of the mountain had more pity on the martyrs of Christ than the pagans had. An angel of God eased the martyrs in their torments; and **the order of the deaths is given** — first the priests and fellow-workers of Athenogenes were beheaded with the sword, and then Athenogenes himself. **ENTRY 4 IS A SECOND ATHENOGENES AND THE BOOK ITSELF MAKES HIM A SECOND MAN.** „Св. муч. Атиноген.“ — „Састављач вечерње песме: Свете тихи. Скончао за Христа у огњу и удостојио се вечне славе у царству Божјем.“ The composer of the evening hymn «O gladsome light»; he ended for Christ in fire and was counted worthy of eternal glory in the kingdom of God. **Two entries of one name on one day of one calendar is two men** — the standing ruling that kept the Prologue’s Egyptian Дула off `doulas-of-cilicia` on 15 June and that the book itself stated in a sentence on 9 July — and the differences are plain: the first Athenogenes is a bishop beheaded with the sword with ten disciples in 311, this one is a hymnographer who died **in fire**. **The nearest folder is refused.** `athenogenes-disciple-of-athenogenes` carries the name, `death` 311, the Greek 16 July and a `related` row to the bishop — and he is **one of the first entry’s ten**, so writing entry 4 onto him would be the exact error the Дула ruling forbids, the same shape as `patermuthius-17-december` on 9 July. `ls saints | grep -i athenogen` returns the bishop and his ten and nobody else. Ruling 3: **reported, not created, and no row for any Athenogenes on entry 4.** The two sentences are reported here and written into no life. **`hymnographer` is therefore refused along with the folder**, there being nothing to put it on. **ENTRY 5 IS REFUSED TWICE OVER AND IS THE FIRST MOVEABLE FEAST OF THIS RANGE.** „Спомен шест Васељенских Сабора.“ — „Овај заједнички спомен првих шест Сабора врши се оне недеље између 13. и 19. јула.“ This common commemoration of the first six Councils is performed **on that Sunday which falls between 13 and 19 July**. First, §4: a Council is not a person, and a heading that enumerates nobody is one entry and the reader says so — this one enumerates nothing but a number. Second, and independently, **a feast that is neither a fixed day nor a Pascha offset cannot be held**: the Sunday between the 13th and the 19th is neither, and the standing ruling is to leave it out and name it. Either refusal would be enough and both apply. **It is also the reason the day’s own number is not what the Prologue is keeping here**, which is worth saying plainly: this book prints the entry under the 16 July because the 16th is the middle of that week, not because the feast falls on the 16th. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Şi părtaş obiceiurilor şi următor scaunelor apostolilor fiind, lucrare ai aflat, de Dumnezeu insuflate, spre suirea privirii la cele înalte. Pentru aceasta, cuvântul adevărului drept învăţând şi cu credinţa răbdând până la sânge Sfinţite Mucenice Atinoghen, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Sfințit Mucenic Atinoghen cu cei 10 ucenici ai săi», Glasul 4 — the common of hieromartyrs, printed there under his name.

english.text: A sharer in their ways and a successor to the apostles' thrones, you found in action, God-inspired one, a way up to the vision of the things on high. Therefore, rightly teaching the word of truth and enduring in faith even to blood, hieromartyr Athenogenes, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Χρῖσμα ἀγιόν, εἰσδεδεγμένος, Μάρτυς ἔνθεος, τοῦ Λόγου ὤφθης, Ἀθηνόγενες ἀθλήσας στερρότατα, καὶ ὡς θυσίαν αὐτῶ προσενήνοχας τῶν φοιτητῶν σου δεκάδα τὴν πάνσεπτον μεθ' ὧν πρέσβευε, δοθήναι τοὶς σὲ γεραίρουσι, πταισμάτων ἱλασμὸν καὶ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ', Θείας πίστεως — the first of two hymns on the page of «Άγιος Αθηνογένης επίσκοπος Πηδαχθόης και οι Δέκα Μαθητές του», and it names him and his decad of students

english.text: Having received the holy chrism, you were shown forth as a martyr filled with God, a martyr of the Word, Athenogenes, having contended most stoutly; and you offered Him as a sacrifice the all-venerable decad of your students. With them, intercede that forgiveness of sins and great mercy be given to those who honour you.

hymns.text: Κανόνα πίστεως, καὶ εἰκόνα πραότητος, ἐγκρατείας διδάσκαλον, ἀνέδειξε σε τῇ ποίμνῃ σου, ἡ τῶν πραγμάτων ἀλήθεια· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκτήσω τῇ ταπεινώσει τὰ ὑψηλά, τῇ πτωχείᾳ τὰ πλούσια. Πάτερ Ἱεράρχα Ἀθηνογένη, πρέσβευε Χριστῷ τῷ θεῷ, σωθῆναι τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ' — the second of two hymns on the page of «Άγιος Αθηνογένης επίσκοπος Πηδαχθόης», printed under his name with his name sung into it; it is the common of a hierarch and is taken as a common

english.text: The truth of things has shown you to your flock as a rule of faith, an image of meekness and a teacher of abstinence; therefore you have gained the heights by humility and riches by poverty. Father and hierarch Athenogenes, intercede with Christ our God that our souls may be saved.

death.note: saint.gr heads him «Αγιος Αθηνογενης Επισκοπος Πηδαχθοης (; - 311)», with no year of birth, and gives the same year to each of the ten disciples in their own headings. Its narrative states no year; the heading is where the year is. doxologia.ro, the folder's other source, gave no year at all and only the reign of Diocletian.
